title: Handshake window SLA: edge vs core latency-dollar collateral (draft)
body:
Purpose
-----
Quick experimental collateral for the "handshake window" SLA knob: when to prefer an edge-proximate fast path versus routing to a stable core pool for conversational workloads. This is a rough draft intended for internal reviews and to form the basis of a one-pager for SRE and Customer Solutions.

Summary (tl;dr)
----------------
- Edge wins for median latency (p50) and first-token latency for short-turn interactive flows, but core is cheaper per-token at sustained high concurrency.
- There is a small sweet spot (window sizes ~150–400ms) where hybrid routing (try-edge-for-window, fallback-to-core) recovers most p50 benefits while bounding cost increase to <12% for our synthetic chat mix.
- Recommendations: expose a single "handshake_window_ms" knob in console, default 200ms; automatic tiering policy that decays to core after N ms or M tokens.

Experimental setup (notes)
--------------------------
- Model: open-llm-v2.1 quantized int8 (same build on edge and core kernels)
- Edge nodes: 2x A10g-like GPUs (low-prox region), prewarmed containers, tiny KV cache configured (100 session entries)
- Core nodes: 8x A100-equivalent, sustained throughput profile, larger KV cache (512 session entries)
- Workload: synthetic chat mix from customer-sim: 65% short-turn (prompt <80 tokens, expected reply 15–60 tokens), 35% long-turn (reply 120–600 tokens). Arrival process: Poisson with bursts (peak factor 6).
- Measurement: p50/p90/p99 first-token latency, tail-after-warm, tokens-per-dollar (TP$) approximated with infra cost model used by Finance (GPU-hours + egress).
- Note: experiments run in parallel across regions for 24 hours to collect microburst traces.

ASCII chart: median latency vs handshake window (ms)
------------------------------------------------
Key: Edge-only (E), Core-only (C), Hybrid (H) = try-edge for window then route to core if not started. Values are p50 first-token latency (ms).

window_ms | E   | C   | H(try)
--------------------------------
0         | 55  | 120 | 120   (H==C when 0)
100       | 58  | 122 | 64    (most edge wins)
200       | 61  | 125 | 68    (good tradeoff)
400       | 66  | 130 | 73    (diminishing returns)
800       | 82  | 140 | 86    (edge throttling visible)

Interpretation: up to ~200ms window the hybrid policy recovers ~80–90% of edge median benefits while keeping long-run fallback behavior tight.

ASCII chart: p90 latency (ms) under peak microburst
-------------------------------------------------
window_ms | E   | C   | H
-----------------------
0         | 150 | 240 | 240
100       | 165 | 245 | 185
200       | 185 | 260 | 200
400       | 230 | 290 | 225
800       | 360 | 340 | 345

Notes: p90 shows core holds better under extreme bursts (stable queue discipline), but hybrid softens edge tails for reasonable windows. At large windows (>=800ms) edge tail explodes (resource contention) and actually surpasses core p90.

Cost sketch (tokens-per-dollar, lower is better cost)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Edge-only baseline: 0.86 TP$ (higher cost due to smaller batch efficiency and smaller GPUs)
- Core-only baseline: 0.35 TP$
- Hybrid (window=200ms): 0.42 TP$ (≈ +20% vs core but -51% vs edge)

Rough tradeoff curve (qualitative):
- 0–150ms: cost increases modestly, latency gains high 
- 150–400ms: knee region — best marginal improvements per cost dollar
- >400ms: tail risk and cost escalate rapidly

Operational considerations and caveats
------------------------------------
- KV cache effectiveness: edge KV hit rate materially affects the window sweet spot. For workloads with high session locality (hit rate > 0.6) edge advantage increases; for low locality the cost delta grows.
- Warmup penalty: we observed a ~30–80ms cold-start/handshake penalty for ephemeral containers if burst exceeds prewarm assumptions. Prewarm policies interact strongly with handshake_window and should be coordinated.
- Regional capacity: fallback to core introduces cross-region egress and routing latency; prefer same-region core or pre-provisioned dedicated core slices for high-SLA customers.
- Instrumentation: need per-route telemetry: handshake_attempts, handshake_success_ms, fallback_reason, cross_region_egress_bytes. Add these to console telemetry table.
- SLO stitching: For customers with p99 SLA targets, hybrid may need stricter window (<=100ms) or reserved capacity to avoid p99 regressions.

Suggested console UX: knobs and defaults
--------------------------------------
- handshake_window_ms: integer, default 200 (expose in route config and RBAC to platform admins).
- fallback_policy: values [immediate-core, windowed, prefer-core] with clear cost/latency hints.
- prewarm_target: percent of edge capacity kept warm (default 15%) with auto-scaling hints.

Open questions / To do
---------------------
- Do we want an automatic adaptive window that shrinks during sustained congestion? (prototype idea: reduce handshake_window_ms when edge cpu_util > 80% for 30s)
- How to present cost impact in the console in an instantly actionable way? Proposed: dynamic estimate of % dollars vs baseline core, shown before applying changes.
- SLA semantics for hybrid: are fallbacks considered "served by core" for billing/attribution? (billing and legal ops need to sign off)

Quick playbook for customer reps
--------------------------------
- If customer cares about interactive feel and p50: recommend handshake_window_ms = 200 and small reserved edge slice. Warn about ~+15–25% unit cost.
- If customer is cost-sensitive and throughput-bound: set handshake_window_ms <= 50 or prefer-core policy.
- If p99 is critical: recommend prefer-core or canary hybrid with heavy p99 monitoring and larger prewarm.

Appendix: short trace example (abridged)
--------------------------------------
Sample request trace (edge route):
- t+0ms: request received at edge proxy (cold? false)
- t+8ms: route decision -> try-edge window=200ms
- t+12ms: container assigned (warm)
- t+58ms: first token emitted -> good
- t+1300ms: long decode continues on edge (resource contended) -> p90 increases

Fallback trace (hybrid):
- t+0ms: request received at edge
- t+120ms: no free slot within window -> route to core (same-region)
- t+240ms: first token from core -> fallback penalty ~240ms but core p90 within SLA

Notes to self: capture a follow-up table with KV hit-rate sensitivity (0.2/0.5/0.8) and a small section on telemetry event names. Also sync with Finance for more precise TP$ numbers (these are quick model outputs).

End of draft.
